issue.title: test_enter_returns_while_xprompt_file_read_is_blocked fails under the full parallel lane, passes in isolation
issue.description:
DISCOVERED BY: bead sase-n7.3 during epic sase-n7 ('Get monitor reconciliation off the ACE startup critical path'), recorded as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP and routed to a task by sase-n7.land on 2026-08-16.

OBSERVATION: tests/ace/tui/test_xprompt_browser_load_keymap.py::test_enter_returns_while_xprompt_file_read_is_blocked failed during phase sase-n7.3's first 'just check', where the scoped lane escalated to the whole suite. The node passed when rerun in isolation, and the phase's second full 'just check' was green. The phase's own diff touched only src/sase/monitor/store.py (a bounded artifact-index query for monitor reconciliation) and tests/monitor/, so the failure is unrelated to the change under test. The same escalated run also failed tests/test_config.py::test_load_merged_config_invalid_yaml_skipped, which was routed separately as a +1 on sase-mv.

CLASS: green in isolation, red only when the whole suite runs in parallel -- the shape sase-ct was retired for. The node exercises the xprompt browser's Enter handler while an xprompt file read is deliberately blocked, so it is timing- and receiver-sensitive by construction, which is the usual signature of process-global state or scheduler contention leaking in from elsewhere in the suite rather than intra-file contention.

SCOPE: reproduce under the full parallel lane (narrow file-scoped 'just test-contention' is NOT sufficient evidence for this class -- see sase-mv, where file-level contention was already green while the full lane was red), identify whether the trigger is a poisoning test or a genuine race in the blocked-read path, fix the leak or make the node robust, then re-measure with the full parallel lane plus 'just selection-health' and tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

IMPACT: an unpredictable red node in 'just check' escalations and 'just check-full', so agents landing unrelated work must hand-triage before landing. Single observation so far; corroborate rather than duplicate if it recurs.
